subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: Moving air carries away water vapour, keeping a steep gradient and increasing transpiration.

questions.q: Why do palisade cells near the top of a leaf contain many chloroplasts?
options: To absorb maximum light for photosynthesis
questions.explain: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts to capture as much light as possible.

questions.q: In which direction(s) can phloem transport substances?
options: Both up and down the plant
questions.explain: Translocation in phloem can move dissolved food in both directions to where it is needed.

questions.q: Why is a plant often kept in the dark before testing a leaf for starch?
options: To destarch the leaf so any new starch comes from the experiment
questions.explain: Destarching ensures any starch found afterwards was made during the test conditions.

questions.q: Why does increasing temperature usually increase transpiration?
options: Water molecules evaporate and diffuse faster
questions.explain: Higher temperatures speed up evaporation and diffusion of water vapour from the leaf.

questions.q: Why does increased light intensity tend to increase transpiration?
options: Stomata open in the light for photosynthesis, allowing more water to escape
questions.explain: In light, stomata open to allow gas exchange for photosynthesis, so more water vapour is lost.

questions.q: Which condition would slow the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: High humidity reduces the concentration gradient of water vapour, slowing transpiration.

questions.q: When testing a leaf for starch, why is the leaf boiled in ethanol?
options: To soften the cell walls only
To remove the chlorophyll so the colour change is visible
questions.explain: Boiling in ethanol removes chlorophyll, so the iodine colour change can be seen clearly.

questions.q: Photosynthesis is described as endothermic because it...
options: transfers energy from the environment (light) into the plant
questions.explain: Photosynthesis takes in light energy, so it is an endothermic reaction.

questions.q: Which of these is a limiting factor for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature can all limit the rate of photosynthesis.

options: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant
The movement of sugars in phloem
questions.explain: Transpiration is the evaporation and loss of water vapour, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.q: Which pigment absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.
